text.tspan: A deployable command-line application that validates, renders, and
manages Aurora models. The CLI is optimized for deterministic,
automatable workflows (local scripting and CI), and delegates model
semantics (parsing, invariants, rendering) to the shared library.
A deployable application that provides an interactive experience for
creating, editing, and navigating Aurora models. The Editor focuses on
discoverability and safe, incremental iteration with immediate
A VS Code extension that enables authoring, validation, and
visualization of Aurora models within the editor. It provides
trust-aware workspace integration, webview-based UI experiences, and
(optionally) an MCP server surface for other in-editor tooling.
Ability to load and save Aurora models from and to disk in stable

Ability to update Aurora models by creating, editing, and deleting

Ability to integrate Aurora tooling with workspace file systems,

Gate potentially unsafe operations (e.g., file writes, webview

Safe Path Handling and Atomic Writes
Constrain paths to the intended workspace/model roots, normalize and
validate paths, and use atomic write patterns to prevent partial writes
Sanitize rendered Markdown and webview content, restrict resource
loading, and disable script execution to prevent injection.
Minimize read/write permissions and scope operations to explicit
user-selected paths; avoid reading or writing unrelated workspace files.

Explain Entire Model in Simple Language
The entire model is expressible by listing the nodes and their
One Model to Rule Them All
A single Aurora model captures every aspect of the architecture in
Express the model in a form that is easy to parse and understand for
The data formats and other elements will be open and uncumbered,
allowing anyone to implement tooling against AURORA.
Provide command line, GUI, and VSCode Extension tools for the AURORA
Tooling surfaces should prioritize shareable, portable artifacts (e.g.,
rendered views and model packages) without compromising workspace trust
There must exist a special card, `Boundary`, with the optional
property `recursive` (default true) which can represent the
containment of other elements without altering the meaning or
relationship of the model; in other words a logical boundary.
There must be a special card called `Note` that allows the capture of
arbitrary text and annotates an existing node in the model without
modifying it or the model. The `Note` card must have only one incoming
link from the card it modifies.
Tools MUST be able to load one or more Aurora models from disk for use
in validation, editing, and rendering workflows.
Tools MUST validate Aurora models against the Aurora schema and
structural invariants, and report actionable diagnostics.
Tools MUST support updating Aurora models, including creating,
editing, and deleting cards and links while preserving model
Tools MUST persist Aurora models to disk in a stable, text-based
representation suitable for diffing and review.
Tools MUST generate human-readable views (e.g., Mermaid diagrams and
Tools MUST be able to emit a compact, machine-friendly representation of
an Aurora model for agent consumption and interchange.
Tools MUST enable users to browse and search the cards and links in an
Tools MUST enable users to create, edit, and delete cards and links
with immediate feedback and without corrupting the model.
Tools MUST surface schema and invariant validation diagnostics in a
form users can act on (including location and remediation hints
Tools MUST provide a graph-based visualization of the model and its
relationships to support navigation and comprehension.
Tools MUST allow users to preview and navigate the human-readable
Markdown renderings generated from an Aurora model.
Tools MUST integrate with the user’s workspace to open, watch, and
save model files using predictable, user-controlled behaviors.
Tools MUST perform file operations safely (prevent unintended
overwrites, constrain paths, and avoid writing outside the
Tools MUST respect workspace trust boundaries by limiting
potentially unsafe operations in untrusted workspaces.
Tools MUST render Markdown and any webview content safely by sanitizing
untrusted content and preventing script injection.
Store the Model in a Postable Format
Tools MUST present the ability to compress the entire model into a
single file (for example, a ZIP) for transport between instances.
Tools MUST render every view defined in the canonical view registry
deterministic set of view outputs for a given model.

Tooling could overwrite or corrupt files outside the intended model
Operating against untrusted workspace content could lead to disclosure
of sensitive data or unintended access beyond user intent.
A bounded system that delivers the default Aurora tooling surfaces:
Untrusted content in model descriptions or rendered Markdown could

A crafted input path or unsafe write behavior could cause tooling to

Operating in an untrusted workspace could allow unsafe operations that
